subject: Nebula Health — dedicated SLO sizing heuristics & demo follow-up
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nebulahealth.com>, Tara Wilson <tara.wilson@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nebula Health performance demo — dedicated sizing discussion

Thanks again for the 60-minute walkthrough today — appreciated the clarity on the workload. Quick recap from our side and a concrete test plan so we can validate reserved capacity sizing for your SLOs.

High-level SLOs you confirmed on the call:
- Latency target: p50 <= 120ms for short interactive prompts (~<=64 tokens, streaming enabled).
- Tail tolerance: p95 <= 350ms for typical user flows (avg 60-100 tokens).
- Concurrency: sustained 200 concurrent active sessions during peak hour; spike to ~450 for short bursts (~10 minutes).
- Throughput expectation: average 9000 tokens/minute during peak windows with short streaming bursts.

Key performance questions we need to validate:
1) Which GPU family gives the best cost/latency tradeoff for your mixed workload (H100 80GB, A100 80GB, or L4 for quantized variants)?
2) How does prefix/KV caching change effective throughput for your conversational patterns?
3) Streaming behavior: how do small-chunk streaming latencies behave under batching vs continuous-kv strategies?
4) Headroom sizing: what reserved throughput we should commit to vs autoscale buffer to meet p95 under bursts?

Proposed validation plan (two-week pilot + bench runs):
A. Bench matrix (run by Redwood infra team; we’ll share harness):
   - Tail-latency single-threaded runs (H100 / A100 / L4) with your prompt set (64, 128, 256 token variants). Capture p50/p95/tail.
   - Sustained throughput runs with continuous batching to measure tokens/sec and GPU utilization for each family.
   - Streaming concurrency simulation: 200 -> 450 concurrent session profile, with 100ms chunk cadence, measure time-to-first-byte and end-to-end p95.
B. Pilot config suggestion (starting point):
   - Reserved slab: 2 x H100-80GB as baseline (reserve), autoscale to 4 H100 for sustained peaks.
   - Baseline reserved throughput target: 800 tokens/sec (tunable after bench).
   - Quantized fallback (4-bit) on L4 for very small prompts/low-cost tier — evaluate accuracy delta.
C. Deliverables:
   - Bench results workbook (p50/p95, tokens/sec, GPU util, KV hit rate, batch sizes).
   - Recommended reserved throughput and autoscale policy with cost delta estimates.

Immediate asks from Nebula to proceed:
- Shared prompt set (anonymized) + representative traffic profile (CSV) — 1 business day.
- Agreement on pilot dates (we can start benching as soon as Wed 9/15).

Attached: demo recording (video) and a short throughput spec sheet.

Next steps:
- If this plan looks ok, we’ll schedule bench window and Ben will spin up the harness. I’ll follow with a Slack invite and access link.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nebulahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tara Wilson <tara.wilson@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nebula Health performance demo — dedicated sizing discussion

Appreciate the detailed recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from procurement/ops side: 
- We need an upfront estimate of cost for the 2-week pilot and for the baseline reserved slab (ballpark per-month). Can you include both (H100 baseline and cheaper L4 fallback)?
- SLA ask: We’ll need 99.9% availability for reserved capacity and a clear escalation path if tail latency slips during our peak.
- Data controls: confirm logs/audit access for the pilot (we need to verify KV cache behavior against our PII redaction).

We’ll prepare the anonymized prompt set. Target to share by EOD Thu 9/14. Pilot starting 9/15 works on our side — want bench results before the week is out.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product Operations | Nebula Health
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nebulahealth.com>, Tara Wilson <tara.wilson@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nebula Health performance demo — dedicated sizing discussion

Thanks Samir — quick responses inline and a concrete pilot proposal: 
- Cost: Ben, can you produce a two-line estimate: (a) 2-week pilot (bench compute + infra) and (b) monthly committed cost for 2 x H100 reserved vs 2 x L4 reserved (we’ll include autoscale delta).
- SLA: Redwood can provide an enterprise SLA for Dedicated — for pilots we provide operational SLAs (response + remediation windows). I’ll surface the 99.9% availability ask to our contracts team and flag for legal if Nebula requests the stronger guarantee for production.
- Logs/audit: we can provide time-limited audit logs for the pilot and enable request-level tracing (no raw PII stored by Redwood unless you route it to our private deployment). We’ll outline the exact log fields in the bench plan document.

Pilot: 2-week (9/15 start)
- Week 1: bench matrix across H100 / A100 / L4; deliver preliminary workbook by end of week.
- Week 2: focused pilot on chosen slab with streaming load pattern and KV caching enabled; capture production-like traces.

Ben & Soojin will run the bench. Ben: can you confirm availability for 9/15 bench run and drop the cost estimate by 12:00 PT? Also adding a few bench metrics we need captured so results are actionable.

Logan
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Bench run checklist & metrics (Nebula pilot)

Internal checklist before 9/15 bench:
- Harness: ensure Nebula prompt set uploaded to test cluster and anonymized keys present.
- GPU matrix: test H100-80GB, A100-80GB, L4 (4-bit quantized) — identical model weights and tokenizer.
- Scenarios:
  * Single-request tail-latency (cold KV, warm KV)
  * Sustained throughput (15 minute steady-state window)
  * Burst profile (200->450 concurrent over 10 minutes)
  * Streaming chunk cadence (50ms / 100ms / 200ms)
- Metrics to capture (per run): p50, p95, p99 latency; median time-to-first-byte; tokens/sec; GPU utilization and memory; batch size distribution; KV cache hit rate; 99th percentile CPU wait.
- Artifacts: bench workbook (CSV + pivot), Grafana screenshot pack, run command snippets, and replay harness link.

Notes: prioritize H100 runs for final recommendation; include an L4 low-cost comparison with measured accuracy delta (per-sample diff) so product can validate.

I will own the run orchestration and the bench workbook. Ben — please attach the cost estimates and I'll include them in the deliverable to Nebula.

— Soojin
